title: Examples
snippet:
The scripts in this guide are in the REST code examples [GitHub repository](https://github.com/googleads/google-ads-rest), including the [`rest_guide` directory](https://github.com/googleads/google-ads-rest/tree/master/rest_guide).
To view the request and response bodies for each API method, refer to the reference documentation for specific service endpoints.
For example, the [reference page](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/rpc/v26/GoogleAdsService/Search?transport=rest) for `GoogleAdsService.Search` shows the request and response bodies for the `Search` method.

title: Search & SearchStream
snippet:
- The Google Ads API provides a unified mechanism for attribute retrieval and metrics reporting using the Google Ads Query Language.
- You can use either the `Search` or `SearchStream` methods to create queries, both supporting the same queries and returning equivalent results.
- The `Search` method returns data in fixed-size pages of 10,000 rows, enabling pagination and suitable for low bandwidth conditions.
- The `SearchStream` method streams the entire result set in a single response, which is more efficient for bulk data retrieval.
The Google Ads API has a unified [attribute retrieval and metrics reporting mechanism](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/reporting/overview) that lets you create queries using the [Google Ads Query Language](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/query/overview). This enables complex queries that can return large quantities of data about individual Google Ads accounts.

Both `Search` and `SearchStream` use the same base URL:
```
https://googleads.googleapis.com/v26/customers/CUSTOMER_ID/googleAds
```
```
POST /v26/customers/CUSTOMER_ID/googleAds:search HTTP/1.1
Host: googleads.googleapis.com
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN
{
"query": "SELECT ad_group_criterion.keyword.text, ad_group_criterion.status FROM ad_group_criterion WHERE ad_group_criterion.type = 'KEYWORD' AND ad_group_criterion.status = 'ENABLED'"
}
```
If there are more than 10,000 rows in the results a `nextPageToken` is returned in the response:
```
{
"results": [
// ...
// ...
// ...
],
"nextPageToken": "CPii5aS87vfFTBAKGJvk36qpLiIWUW5SZk8xa1JPaXJVdXdIR05JUUpxZyoCVjMwADjUBkD___________8B",
"fieldMask": "adGroupCriterion.keyword.text,adGroupCriterion.status"
}
```

title: REST Interface Design
snippet:
- The Google Ads API generally follows a resource-oriented design, modeled as collections of individually-addressable resources that are referenced with their resource names and manipulated using a small set of methods.
- Resource names and methods, combined with a specific API version prefix, comprise the URLs of the REST interface.

- A discovery document is available for each version of the API to facilitate and automate the discovery of available methods.

## Resource-oriented design
Generally, the Google Ads API follows a resource-oriented design, modeled as *collections* of individually-addressable *resources* (the *nouns* of the API). Resources are referenced with their resource names and manipulated using a small set of *methods* (also known as *verbs* or *operations*). These [resource names](/google-ads/api/rest/design/resource-names) and [methods](/google-ads/api/rest/design/service-methods), combined with a specific *API version prefix*, comprise the URLs of the REST interface. For example, this example URL can be broken down into these individual components according to the following table:
```
https://googleads.googleapis.com/v26/customers/1234567890:mutate
```
| API Version Prefix | Resource Name (relative) | Method |
|---|---|---|
| `https://googleads.googleapis.com/v26` | `customers/1234567890` | `mutate` |
All REST URLs for a particular version of the API (e.g., `v26`) share a common API version prefix. The resource name and method together identifies which API service is being called.
The Google Ads API makes heavy use of *custom methods*, as opposed to most REST APIs that use standard REST methods such as `list`, `get`, `create`, `update`, and `delete`. Examples of custom methods in the Google Ads API include `search`, `searchStream`, and `mutate`.
The following pages go into more details about the Google Ads API's [resource names](/google-ads/api/rest/design/resource-names), [service methods](/google-ads/api/rest/design/service-methods), and [JSON naming conventions](/google-ads/api/rest/design/json-mappings) to illustrate how they're used together to define REST interface endpoints.

## Discovery document
To facilitate and automate the discovery of available methods in the Google Ads API, you can use the discovery document published for each version.
